name: pg_duckdb
tagline: PostgreSQL extension that embeds DuckDB's vectorized engine for fast analytics and data-lake queries.
description: pg_duckdb is the official DuckDB extension for PostgreSQL, built by DuckDB Labs with MotherDuck and Hydra. It embeds DuckDB inside the Postgres process so analytical queries over Postgres tables can be executed by DuckDB's columnar, vectorized engine, often orders of magnitude faster than the Postgres executor for scans and aggregations. It can also read and write Parquet, CSV, JSON, Iceberg and Delta Lake files on S3, GCS, Azure and R2, and optionally offload work to MotherDuck. It reached 1.0 in September 2025 and supports current PostgreSQL majors including 18; it complements Postgres for analytics rather than replacing a warehouse.

pricing.notes: Free; optional MotherDuck integration is billed by MotherDuck.

scale.notes: Runs inside a single Postgres server; can push compute to MotherDuck for larger data.

strengths: DuckDB's vectorized execution accelerates analytical queries on Postgres tables
Query Parquet, Iceberg and Delta Lake on object storage directly from SQL
No data movement to a separate warehouse for moderate analytics
Backed by the DuckDB core team
weaknesses: Analytics still run on the OLTP server and compete for its resources
Not available on most hyperscaler managed Postgres services
Type and function mismatches between DuckDB and Postgres need care
Release cadence slowed after 1.1 (last release December 2025)
useCases: Dashboards and reports directly on Postgres data
Joining Postgres tables with Parquet/Iceberg data in S3
Exporting query results to Parquet for data lakes
Ad-hoc analytics without standing up a warehouse
notIdealFor: Managed Postgres platforms that do not allow custom extensions
